analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Own Judgement. Compartmentalized. Dollar Longs 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: Asia was softer overnight. Nikkei fell 0.94% after a 3.3% gain the prior day, Korea was roughly flat, and Hong Kong fell 2.7%. The author reads the Hong Kong drop as technical, driven by the reopening after a holiday with Southbound Stock Connect shut for Golden Week. Financials led, with HSBC and AIA down about 5% against tech at about -2%.

US equities absorbed a rates shock that hit Europe. Treasuries sold off hard and OAT/Bund passed 130bp. Stress then reached Italian BTPs. The S&P barely moved, and the Nasdaq and Russell finished green.

Fed: Jefferson said inflation is still too high with upside risks, but that colleagues will need to reach their own judgment on the next move, which may take more time. With tighter financial conditions from higher yields, this is a second Fed voice (after Williams) against following through automatically in October. October pricing has come down, but another hike later in the year remains possible.

France is the center of the European rates stress. BTPs moved with OATs for the first time in this episode, which the author takes as the market starting to price European sovereign risk rather than only French fiscal risk. Italy has a primary surplus and a smaller deficit, helped by EU recovery funds. The author reads a French political premium building, since a future government could put domestic spending ahead of EU constraints. The author also sees more bearish euro and long dollar flow, and asks how disorderly contagion must get before ECB speakers talk up support.

AI compute remains scarce and pricing is firm. AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks for machine learning by about 15% effective October 7, 2026, its fourth consecutive quarterly increase, and A100 instances are included for the first time since January.

AI financing is getting more complex. Amazon is reportedly looking at moving about $8bn of Nvidia GPUs into an SPV, selling it to outside investors and leasing the chips back. The author does not read this as collateral worry. Broadcom lending up to $42bn to support leases of compute built around its own chips is the one the author likes less, because the supplier is financing the customer buying its product. Circularity is rising but the author says it is not today's problem.

Oil: alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers appear to be moving meaningful barrels despite continued tanker attacks. The durable effect looks like a shipping cost and risk premium rather than lost barrels. Brent backwardation has eased but spot keeps rising, which the author attributes to the cost of delivering cargo. The US deployed another carrier force while diplomacy is stuck, and the author sees the window for an easy off-ramp narrowing. Diesel is the key second-order inflation channel.

Manufacturing data was stronger than the headline ISM miss suggests. New orders, backlogs and employment accelerated, inventories are very low, and S&P PMI hit its highest since May 2022. ISM prices paid rose from 71.1 to 77.9. The author reads this as reacceleration into a supply constraint, not stagflation. It is good for near-term production but implies stickier goods inflation and less room for rates to fall.

NFP: with rates the epicenter, the author wants to avoid both tails. A hot payroll print or accelerating average hourly earnings could put an October hike back in play, and a very weak print could create a growth problem. The author's sweet spot is modest job creation with contained wages, consistent with companies growing top lines without adding headcount.

Risk view: the author remains constructive. Gross exposure still looks robust, AI is performing, and Europe and the Russell have already derated sharply. At current real rates it is getting harder to press shorts. Earnings are growing faster than multiples, which have compressed. Absent a radical breakdown in rates, a modicum of stability could let equities rise quickly. The author expects a middling payroll outcome, vol coming out and a grind into the weekend.

France and European sovereign contagion, with OATs structurally challenged and BTPs now dragged in.
Oil and shipping: tanker attacks, freight and insurance costs, and diesel as a second-order inflation channel.

vol_and_positioning: Rates vol has blown out while US equity vol is expected to come out into the weekend if payrolls land in the middle.
The author sees a notable pickup in bearish euro and long dollar flow.
Gross exposure is described as incredibly robust. Europe and the Russell have had large relative derating, and at current real rates it is getting harder to press shorts.
geopolitical: Continued tanker attacks around the Gulf with alternative routes and ship-to-ship transfers moving barrels, and Hormuz risk raising freight and insurance costs.
The US deployed another carrier force to the region while diplomacy remains stuck, and the author sees the window for an easy off-ramp narrowing.
French political risk. The author sees a political premium building because a future government may prioritize domestic spending over EU constraints, with contagion reaching Italian BTPs.

tension_points.bull_case: Modest job creation with contained wages is the sweet spot, consistent with corporates growing top lines without adding headcount. This keeps inflation worries contained and October off the table.
tension_points.bear_case: A hot payroll print or accelerating average hourly earnings forces an October hike back into play. A very low NFP could instead create a growth problem.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Accelerating average hourly earnings or a hot payroll print that forces October back into play, or a very low NFP that creates a growth problem.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings are moving too fast and multiples have compressed. Gross exposure is robust, AI is delivering, and a modicum of stability could lift equities quickly.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates vol, French and Italian sovereign stress, oil, circular AI financing and payrolls could each break the compartmentalization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A radical breakdown on the rates side.
